description: the frustum of sweep/revolve-frustum grown to z ∈ [−2, 2] — the cone r = 3 − z/2 about z, bored to r = 1 — cut by a half-space tilted by `tilt` about x through the origin, so the cut plane z = y·tan(tilt) meets the cone in a whole ellipse clear of both caps and the apex, and the bore in a second one. The ellipse is the first section an operand's cone face carries: no exact Curve2 on a cone, so its pcurve there is fitted over the cone's own projection and crosses the seam (ADR-0021). The volume is the bored frustum 100π/3 less the piece above the plane: the annulus 1 ≤ r ≤ 2 contributes 3π(2 − 0) and the cone's own cap ∫(6 − 2r − cy) over r ≥ 2, which is 144π/(4 − c²)^(3/2) + 32π/3 − 24π with c = tan(tilt), by ∫dθ/(2 + c·sinθ)² = 4π/(4 − c²)^(3/2); the area is the bottom annulus, the bore, the oblique face (its xy projection over cos tilt) and what is left of the cone, whose element is √5·r·dr·dθ. The oracle's numbers are its own; its reading of Arris's STEP is held to 1e-6, because Open CASCADE's STEP reader drops the fitted pcurve the cone's ellipse is written with — degree five over thirty-six poles — and reprojects it as a cubic over twenty-five, whose (u, v) region is 9.5e-7 of the cone face away from the one Arris measures to 4e-10 of the closed form above
